title: Follow-up: source discovery indexes untracked .claude/worktrees review checkouts
description: Found during GCLI-10 (2026-10-21), off the plan and not a GCLI-10 regression: the DEC-208 standing review worktrees under .claude/worktrees/ are untracked and not ignored, so the DEC-216 slice-1 discovery selection (git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard) lists their source copies. Evidence on this host: 'glyph callers buildIndex' in glyph-cli exits 2 reporting two matches, the second at .claude/worktrees/review-34-ccb30ef/src/indexer.ts, and '--file src/indexer.ts' cannot narrow it because that path contains the pattern. 'glyph impact ... --ref HEAD' is unaffected because a ref indexes the commit's tree. Review worktrees are local scratch and are never committed, so the proposed remedy is one line in .gitignore -- '.claude/worktrees/' -- which makes Git (and therefore discovery) exclude them; a discovery-level exclusion instead would need a design ruling, because slice 1 deliberately follows Git's own answer rather than a local directory list. Working-tree answers in this repository are the only surface affected; CI and --ref answers are already clean.
plan: Add .claude/worktrees/ to .gitignore, with a comment naming DEC-208 review worktrees as local scratch.
Add a discovery test: an untracked, ignored directory holding a duplicate source file contributes nothing, while an unignored one still does (the existing DEC-216 behavior).
Prove the evidence case: on this repository, glyph callers buildIndex resolves to the single src/indexer.ts symbol and glyph diff/callers otherwise answer as before.
bun run check, Docs and Tracker integrity green on the PR head; README or ADR text only if the behavior is stated anywhere (it is Git-ignore semantics already).
